newsitem.title: BULGARIA: STATE CONTRIBUTION RAISES BULGARIA BOURSE CAPITAL.
newsitem.headline: STATE CONTRIBUTION RAISES BULGARIA BOURSE CAPITAL.

text.p: The Bulgarian Stock Exchange (BSE) decided to raise capital to 199 million levs from 100 million levs by allowing the state to contribute for the whole amount of the rise, a BSE official said on Monday.
"The shareholders' meeting decided to raise capital to 199 million levs, allowing the state to acquire some 49 percent of the bourse," the official told reporters.
The decision to allow the state as a shareholder might be considered as an initial step towards launching a centralised stock exchange and developing a capital market in Bulgaria, the official added.
Under another shareholders' decision the BSE was renamed to Bulgarian Stock Exchange-Sofia. The BSE will hold some 51 percent equity in the new institution.
The state will acquire its 49 percent stake by contributing a building in Sofia where the BSE-Sofia will be based. The BSE assets were now valued at 1.01 billion levs.

The shareholders also authorised the BSE board to open subscribtion for a further capital rise to 300 million levs by October 1, allowing shareholders of another bourse, the Sofia Stock Exchange (SSE), to acquire up to 18,000 shares in the BSE-Sofia at par value against their current stakes in the SSE.

The remaining 83,000 shares of the planned further capital rise with a par of 83 million levs will be offered to other investors at a minimum acceptable price of 10,000 levs, the shareholders decided.
Under the BSE-Sofia statutes aprroved by the shareholders a package of 1,000 shares will provide one brokerage seat.

The shareholders elected a new board of directors which includes Plamen Oresharki, a deputy finance minister, Marin Marinov, a deputy industry minister and Georgi Prohaski, financial adviser to the deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov, as representatives of the state in BSE-Sofia.

BSE executive director Viktor Papazov, Dimitar Zhelev, executive director of Bulgaria Holding, Stoyan Alexandrov, executive director of the Central Co-operative Bank, State Savings Bank chairman Spas Dimitrov, Penyo Hadzhiev, executive director of the Bulgarian Investment Bank and Ivanka Petkova were elected as board members.
The BSE-Sofia was expected to start operations at the beginning of September after it gets a licence from Bulgaria's Securities and Stock Exchanges Commission. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
